name: Mythos Wald / Forest Worlds (Gasometer Oberhausen)
times: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, daily in NRW school holidays
ticketNote: Adult €14, reduced €11; online tickets carry a small fee but give priority entry
highlights: Forests from the Amazon to the Congo told in giant photographs inside the 117-metre gasholder, topped by the 35-metre art installation The Tree and the Global Sunrise light-and-sound show.
tip: Take the glass lift to the roof platform for the Ruhr panorama, and combine with Centro Oberhausen next door.
train: Oberhausen Hbf then bus to Neue Mitte
why: The Gasometer's shows are the biggest walk-in spectacle in NRW, and the sunrise light show is made for Anne.

name: Niki de Saint Phalle: Dream Machine (Kunstpalast)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Thu until 21:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €17, under 18 free; choose a visit date in the ticket shop
highlights: Over 100 works in twelve themed rooms covering four decades of Niki de Saint Phalle's Nanas, shooting paintings, films and architecture, including collaborations with Tinguely and Rauschenberg.
tip: Thursday evenings until 21:00 are quiet; the Rheinpark and Rhine tower are a short walk away.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then tram 701 or 705 to Kunstpalast
why: Colourful, joyful, feminist and big enough to fill a day, with free entry for Alma.

name: Yayoi Kusama retrospective (Stedelijk)
times: Daily 10:00-18:00, last entry 17:45
ticketNote: Museum entry €22.50 plus a Kusama surcharge (also for Museumkaart holders); ticket with a fixed start time for the exhibition, sells out
highlights: Seven decades of Kusama with polka dots, mirror rooms and a newly created immersive installation, organised with Fondation Beyeler and Museum Ludwig; works never shown in Europe before.
tip: Buy start-time tickets as soon as you pick a date, go for the first slot of the day, and allow queue time at the mirror rooms.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then tram 2 or 12 to Museumplein
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: The mirror rooms are the most Instagrammed art on earth, and this is the retrospective's final European stop.

name: Franz Marc (K20 Düsseldorf)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, first Wednesday until 22:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: K20 collection and exhibition €17, under 18 free; time-slot tickets required for Franz Marc
highlights: Major Franz Marc exhibition of the Blue Rider painter's animals and colour symbolism at the K20, whose own collection holds Klee, Picasso and Pollock.
tip: Book a time slot online; the first Wednesday of the month is free from 18:00 during the KPMG art evening.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then U-Bahn to Heinrich-Heine-Allee
dateNote: Start date from kunstsammlung.de; end date 24 January 2027 from the NRW tourism board's exhibition listing.
why: Blue horses and yellow cows that children recognise, in one of Germany's top modern art museums an hour away.

name: ASIA POP (NRW-Forum Düsseldorf)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Thu until 21:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €11, reduced €8, under 18 free
highlights: First comprehensive German exhibition on East Asian pop culture, 400 works over 1,200 m2 on K-pop, J-pop, anime, games, fashion and food, with game stations, selfie spots and a karaoke room.
tip: Go on a Thursday evening and finish in Düsseldorf's Japanese quarter on Immermannstrasse for ramen.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then tram 701 or 705 to Kunstpalast
why: A whole exhibition on fandom and K-pop with a karaoke room, an hour from home and free for Alma.

name: William Kentridge: I am not me, the horse is not mine (Bozar)
times: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €20, under 18 free, museumPASSmusées €2; combo with Jean Brusselmans retrospective €28
highlights: Forty years of Kentridge drawings, animated films, sculptures and stage work as Bozar's first Grand Invité, with site-specific pieces and a season of performances.
tip: Add the €8 combo for the Jean Brusselmans retrospective on the same ticket (until 31 January 2027).
train: Brussels Central, 5 minutes on foot
lez: Brussels LEZ: diesel Euro 5 and older and petrol Euro 2 and older banned
why: Kentridge's charcoal animations are a crowd favourite worldwide and this takeover of Bozar is his largest Belgian show.

name: Cosplay: the exhibition (Design Museum Den Bosch)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-17:00, first Thursday also 19:00-22:00
ticketNote: Adult €15, age 18-30 €7.50, under 18 and Museumkaart free
highlights: First large-scale museum exhibition on cosplay in Europe, with dozens of costumes lent by cosplayers in an immersive design by Bart Hess, treating cosplay as a global youth culture.
tip: Check the agenda for cosplay duo tours and dress-up days, which are free with a museum ticket.
train: 's-Hertogenbosch station, 10 minutes on foot
why: A museum show built with the cosplay community is the closest thing to a fan convention Alma can see in a museum.

name: Chez Matisse: Masterpieces from Centre Pompidou (H'ART)
times: Daily 10:00-17:00, last entry 16:30
ticketNote: Adult €29.50 plus an exhibition surcharge, under 18 free; time-slot reservation, book online in advance
highlights: More than 80 works from the Centre Pompidou while Paris is closed, including Matisse's rarely loaned La Blouse roumaine, plus Picasso, Rothko and Newman.
tip: Go on a weekday afternoon; the museum is a short walk from Waterlooplein metro and far less crowded than Museumplein.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then metro 51/53/54 to Waterlooplein
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: Pompidou masterpieces that would otherwise be locked away until 2030, on loan an hour's train from Limburg instead of in Paris.

name: Along the Color Line: 50 years Museum Ludwig
times: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Ticketed via the museum webshop
highlights: The museum's 50th-anniversary survey on the Black diaspora and European modernism, from the Harlem Renaissance to today, with many international loans alongside its own Picasso and Pop collection.
tip: Park at Parkhaus Am Dom and see the cathedral next door; the Ludwig's Picasso floor is included.
train: Köln Hbf, 2 minutes on foot
why: The anniversary show of one of Europe's great modern art museums, an hour from home.

name: L'Impressionnisme, une histoire belge (La Boverie Liège)
times: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, last entry 16:30, closed Monday
ticketNote: Ticketed via shop.infinitix.be; allow 1h30
highlights: Nearly 150 masterpieces from more than 30 museums, including the Musée d'Orsay, pairing Monet, Renoir and Sisley with Ensor, Van Rysselberghe, Anna Boch and Emile Claus for La Boverie's tenth anniversary.
tip: Forty-five minutes from home; go on a weekday morning and lunch in the Parc de la Boverie.
parking: Paid parking at the Médiacité shopping centre across the river
why: Orsay-level Impressionists 45 minutes from Hoensbroek, the biggest art show Liège has staged since Toutankhamon.

name: Willem de Kooning at work (Rijksmuseum)
ticketNote: Adult €25 (€26.50 from 1 Jan 2027), under 19 free; book a dated online ticket, exhibition included in museum entry
highlights: Retrospective of over 120 De Kooning works spanning 65 years, made with the Art Institute of Chicago, with Woman I and Woman and Bicycle hung in the Gallery of Honour next to Rembrandt.
tip: Book the 09:00 slot and see the Night Watch and the Gallery of Honour before the crowds, then the De Kooning rooms.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then tram 2 or 12 to Rijksmuseum
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: The Rijksmuseum rarely gives its Gallery of Honour to a 20th-century painter, and this is the biggest De Kooning show in Europe in years.

name: Thyssen-Bornemisza x Mauritshuis: Masterpieces from Madrid
ticketNote: Included in the regular museum ticket, Museumkaart valid; book a dated online ticket
highlights: 25 masterpieces from the Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid, from Van Eyck and Dürer to El Greco, Bronzino and Piero della Francesca, hung among Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and Rembrandt.
tip: Visit on a Monday afternoon when the Mauritshuis opens at 13:00 and is quietest.
train: Den Haag Centraal, 10 minutes on foot
dateNote: Start date 15 October 2026 per the official Den Haag tourism agenda; the museum page says autumn 2026. The mauritshuis.nl site blocked automated access, so the Dutch museum association listing is cited.
why: A one-time swap that puts Madrid's old masters in the same small building as the Girl with a Pearl Earring.

name: Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor (Van Gogh Museum)
times: Daily 09:00-18:00 (check site, Fridays often later)
ticketNote: Adult €25 (€26 from 1 Jan 2027), under 18 free; online time-slot ticket only, popular slots sell out days ahead
highlights: First Dutch retrospective of James McNeill Whistler, the Victorian dandy behind Whistler's Mother and the Nocturnes, shown alongside the permanent Van Gogh collection.
tip: Book a weekday morning slot weeks ahead; weekends and school holidays sell out well in advance.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then tram 2 or 12 to Van Baerlestraat
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: A Whistler retrospective has never been shown in the Netherlands, and it comes bundled with the world's largest Van Gogh collection.

name: Signac: Symphony of Colours (Kunsthal Rotterdam)
ticketNote: Online ticket with a start time required for everyone, including Museumkaart holders
highlights: Large Neo-Impressionist overview of Paul Signac with harbour scenes, landscapes and portraits, plus Cross and Toorop, organised with Museum Barberini Potsdam and featuring Le port de Rotterdam.
tip: Park in the Museumpark garage and walk over to the Depot Boijmans next door for its rooftop.
train: Rotterdam Centraal then tram 8 or metro to Eendrachtsplein
lez: Rotterdam milieuzone applies to older diesel vehicles
why: The biggest Pointillist show in the Netherlands in years, in a museum that is easy to do with kids.

name: Ossip Zadkine and Belgium (KMSKA Antwerp)
ticketNote: Adult €20 including the permanent collection
highlights: Sixty years after his death, Zadkine's Cubist sculpture is shown with works by his wife Valentine Prax and his Belgian contemporaries, including The Misery of Job which he gave to the museum.
tip: Go on a Thursday for KMSKA LATE with music and performances until 22:00.
train: Antwerpen-Centraal then tram 4 to Museum
lez: Antwerp LEZ: diesel Euro 5 and older banned, registration required for foreign plates
why: The reopened KMSKA is one of Europe's finest museum buildings and this is its main winter show.

train: Köln Messe/Deutz station is at the fair entrance
ticketNote: Day tickets online; an ART COLOGNE ticket also admits you to the Kölner Museumsnacht on 7 November
name: ART COLOGNE
highlights: The 59th edition of the world's oldest art fair: galleries of modern and contemporary art from around the world, combined on Saturday 7 November with the Cologne Museum Night.
tip: Go on Saturday 7 November, see the fair from 11:00 and use the same ticket for the Museumsnacht in the evening.
why: The oldest art fair in the world, an hour away, with a free museum night thrown in this weekend.

name: Jumping Indoor Maastricht 2026
times: Thu 5: JIM Cup finals and Limburgse Avond; Fri 6: CSI4* and Driving World Cup warm-up; Sat 7: Jimmy Afternoon 13:00-15:30, Big Tour 19:30, Driving World Cup final 21:45; Sun 8: Grand Prix of Maastricht 14:30
ticketNote: Day tickets via Ticketcrew; Saturday evening and Sunday Grand Prix are the premium sessions.
highlights: A CSI4* show jumping week with the FEI Driving World Cup four-in-hand final on Saturday night, the Grand Prix of Maastricht on Sunday and a family 'Jimmy Afternoon' with pony classes and a meet and greet on Saturday.
tip: Take the Saturday afternoon family session and stay for the floodlit Driving World Cup at 21:45; MECC is 15 minutes from home.
why: Top-level show jumping and the carriage-driving World Cup, 15 minutes from home.

name: GLOW Eindhoven 2026
ticketNote: Free; only the drone show at Philips Stadion needs a 2 euro timed ticket
highlights: Around 30 light-art installations on a 5 km walking route through the centre, with a first-ever drone show at the Philips Stadion and satellite works in Helmond, Veldhoven, Best, Oirschot and Laarbeek.
tip: Come on a weekday, arrive by train at Eindhoven Centraal or Strijp-S, and book the 2 euro drone-show slot in advance; the centre is closed to through traffic from 18:00.
parking: Reserve via ParkingYou (up to 15 euro per day, 20 euro walk-up); P+R Evoluon with bus 401/402/403
train: Eindhoven Centraal and Strijp-S are both on the route
why: The biggest light-art festival in the Netherlands is one hour away and free, so the whole family can walk it on a school night.
dateNote: Theme 2026: CONNECT. Satellite towns close at 22:00.

ticketNote: Standard tickets sold out; last-minute tickets only for Uitpas holders while stocks last
name: Museumnacht Amsterdam
highlights: Dozens of Amsterdam museums open until 2:00 with DJs, performances and workshops on one ticket.
tip: This edition is sold out; set a reminder for ticket sales for the 2027 edition in early autumn.
why: A night of museums turned into clubs is the kind of teen-friendly spectacle Alma would enjoy.

times: Special Last Post around 11:00; evening Last Post 20:00; Great War Remembered concert 17:00
venue: Menin Gate Memorial and St Martin's Cathedral
ticketNote: Ceremonies free; concert tickets EUR 34-59
dateNote: 11 November is fixed; the Last Post Association confirms the 11 Nov 2026 concert. Ceremony times follow the usual Armistice Day pattern.
name: Armistice Day at the Menin Gate, Ypres
highlights: Belgium's national Armistice commemoration under the restored Menin Gate, with a special Last Post with massed buglers and pipers, poppy petals, wreath-laying and the Last Post Association's Great War Remembered concert in the cathedral.
tip: Arrive at the Gate well before 10:00 for the morning ceremony or by 19:00 for the evening Last Post; the Market Square screens the ceremony live.
why: The most moving Armistice Day ceremony in Europe, two hours from home at the gate that bears 54,000 names.

name: Thomas Schütte (K21 Düsseldorf)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: K21 collection and exhibition €15, under 18 free; combined K20+K21 ticket €21
highlights: Comprehensive show made with the Düsseldorf sculptor fresh from his MoMA retrospective, with monumental figures such as Vater Staat and Mutter Erde and the first full overview of his architectural models.
tip: Climb into Tomás Saraceno's in orbit net under the K21 glass dome while you are there.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then tram to Graf-Adolf-Platz
why: A home-town survey of one of the most important living sculptors, straight after his MoMA show.

ticketNote: Theme-park tickets from €39 online; prices rise with demand
name: Phantasialand Wintertraum
highlights: The park opens until 20:00 with a sea of lights, seven winter shows and the nightly Magic Symphony closing show of music, light and effects.
tip: Arrive after 14:00 on a weekday for cheaper tickets and the lit-up evening, and stay for Magic Symphony at closing.
why: A theme park in full winter lights with a nightly light-and-music finale, an hour from home.

times: Live on NPO 3 from 12:00
dateNote: Date and city as announced by the NTR and reported by Hart van Nederland/ANP; the NTR Sinterklaasjournaal site is script-rendered so the announcement could not be quoted from the official page directly.
ticketNote: Free
name: Landelijke intocht Sinterklaas
highlights: Sinterklaas and the Pieten sail up the Maas into the fortress town of Grave for the national televised arrival, followed by a procession through the town.
tip: Arrive before 11:00 to get a spot on the quay; the town is small and fills early, so use the signed parking fields outside and expect a walk.
why: The national Sinterklaas arrival happens only an hour from home this year.

ticketNote: Date tickets online; prices vary by day and are not listed on the event page
name: Winter Efteling
highlights: The fairytale park dressed for winter: the Warme Winter Weide with fires and lights, illuminated Symbolica, coasters running weather permitting and evening shows.
tip: Pick a weekday in late November or January to avoid the Christmas-holiday crowds, and stay until dark for the lights.
why: The Efteling in winter lights is a classic family day ninety minutes from home.

name: Voyage à l'anglaise: William Turner and the Grand Tour (Lille)
times: Mon 14:00-18:00, Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed Tuesday
ticketNote: Full price €7, reduced €4
highlights: Turner and the artists of the Grand Tour in France's second-largest fine arts museum, shown as its renovated first floor partly reopens.
tip: Park at Euralille and walk; Lille's Christmas market on Place Rihour runs through December for the same trip.
train: Lille Flandres, 10 minutes on foot
why: Turner loans at a €7 ticket price, in a city that makes a good winter weekend.

name: Amsterdam Light Festival 2026-27 (Edition 15)
times: Lights on 16:30-23:00 daily (31 Dec until 21:00)
venue: Canals of the city centre, 4.5 km walking route
ticketNote: Walking route is free; canal boat tours (about 75 min) are ticketed through official partners
highlights: Light artworks by international artists float above and along the canals for seven weeks; see them on foot on a 4.5 km route or from an official canal boat.
tip: Book a boat tour on a weekday evening well ahead for the Christmas holidays, and pick up the festival app in mid-November for the walking route.
train: Amsterdam Centraal, then walk or metro to Waterlooplein (info point at Amstel 1)
lez: Amsterdam has a milieuzone for older diesel cars; take the train
why: A world-class light festival that works as a winter weekend trip and combines a free canal walk with a boat tour.

dateNote: Runs 28 November to 16 December 2026 and 6 to 17 January 2027 on Wednesdays and weekends; the day list assumes Wed/Sat/Sun within those windows, confirm on toverland.com.
ticketNote: Free entry with a free reservation; pay per ride
name: Toverland Winter Feelings
highlights: Toverland opens its indoor and winter areas free of charge on winter Wednesdays and weekends with pay-per-ride attractions, lights and winter food.
tip: Reserve the free ticket online, go after 15:00 for the lights and budget for a handful of rides rather than a day pass.
why: A free winter evening at the nearest theme park, forty minutes from home.

name: Jacques Tilly: Resistance on Parade (Kunstmuseum Bonn)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Wed until 19:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €10, reduced €5
highlights: Original models, sketches and films of Jacques Tilly's political Rosenmontag floats, the satirical giants that go viral from Düsseldorf's carnival parade every year.
tip: See it before Rosenmontag (8 February 2027) and then catch the real floats in Düsseldorf or Köln.
train: Bonn Hbf then U-Bahn to Heussallee/Museumsmeile
why: For a family that loves parades, this is the workshop behind the most famous carnival floats in Germany.

name: Vanguardistas: 100 Years of Latin American Women Artists
ticketNote: Adult €14 combined ticket for all exhibitions, under 19 free; online tickets skip the till
highlights: First European survey of more than 70 Latin American women artists over a century, from Frida Kahlo and Tarsila do Amaral to Doris Salcedo, with works never shown in Europe.
tip: Wednesday evenings until 21:00 are quiet; the Museumsmeile has the Haus der Geschichte for Nick next door, free.
train: Bonn Hbf then U-Bahn 16/63/66 to Heussallee/Museumsmeile
why: Frida Kahlo in Bonn, in a survey nobody in Europe has attempted before.

times: Museum sites 09:30-18:00; town programme Saturday
venue: Bastogne War Museum, Bastogne War Rooms, Bois Jacques and town centre
ticketNote: Free (museum activities free except the four immersive experiences)
name: Nuts Weekend Bastogne 2026 (Battle of the Bulge commemoration)
highlights: The 82nd anniversary of the Siege of Bastogne: historic military vehicles, living-history camps, battlefield walks in the Bois Jacques and the traditional town parade where nuts are thrown into the crowd, recalling McAuliffe's 'Nuts!' reply.
tip: Come on the Saturday for the town parade and convoys, dress for Ardennes cold, and park early as the centre closes to traffic.
why: The biggest Battle of the Bulge commemoration in the Ardennes, with American veterans' units, convoys and re-enactors filling Bastogne.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup Antwerpen 2026
ticketNote: Day tickets through the World Cup ticket shop.
highlights: The Scheldecross on the sandy Scheldt beach opposite the Antwerp skyline, the first of two Belgian World Cup rounds on the same weekend.
tip: Combine it with the Antwerp Christmas market; take the Sint-Anna tunnel on foot from the old town.
lez: Antwerp has a low-emission zone; register your car or park on Linkeroever outside the zone.
why: A World Cup cross on a city beach with the Antwerp skyline behind it.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup Koksijde 2026
venue: Dunes of the Koksijde air base
ticketNote: Day tickets through the World Cup ticket shop.
highlights: The Duinencross, the most famous sand race in cyclocross, run through the dunes of the former Koksijde military air base.
tip: Stand on the big dune behind the pits where the riders fight through deep sand; wear boots.
why: The legendary dune cross on a Belgian air base, on the Sunday after Antwerp.

name: Superprestige Heusden-Zolder 2026
ticketNote: Day tickets usually around EUR 15-20 at the circuit.
highlights: The Christmas Day cyclocross on the Zolder race circuit, a Belgian family tradition with the full Superprestige field and beer tents in the paddock.
tip: Go after Christmas lunch; the elite men start mid-afternoon and the circuit car parks are plentiful.
why: A Christmas Day cyclocross 45 minutes from home on a motor racing circuit.
dateNote: Friday 25 December 2026 per the published 2026-27 Belgian cyclocross calendar (Sporza); the organiser's site could not be reached from this session to confirm.

name: Jumping Mechelen 2026 (Vlaanderens Kerstjumping)
ticketNote: Tickets via the organiser; the World Cup jumping evening on 30 December sells out first.
highlights: Belgium's Christmas jumping: FEI World Cup legs in jumping, dressage and driving between Christmas and New Year, with show acts and a packed Nekkerhal every evening.
tip: Book the final evening for the World Cup Grand Prix and arrive early for the Christmas market in Mechelen's Grote Markt.
lez: Mechelen has a low-emission zone in the centre; the Nekkerhal has its own car parks outside it.
why: Christmas-week World Cup show jumping with show-business flair, 90 minutes away.
dateNote: 26-30 December 2026 per ClipMyHorse event listings; the organiser's site could not be reached from this session, dates follow the fixed 26-30 December pattern of every edition.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup Namur 2026
times: Women elite 13:40, men elite 15:10
ticketNote: EUR 20.50 presale, EUR 25 on the day; children born 2014 or later free.
highlights: The toughest course on the World Cup calendar, up and down the ramparts of the Namur citadel with its famous off-camber descent, between Christmas and New Year.
tip: Stand on the off-camber section below the citadel wall for the crashes and walk up early because the citadel paths get crowded.
why: The most spectacular cyclocross course in the world, on a fortress 75 minutes from home.

name: Superprestige Diegem 2026
times: Evening races under floodlights, men elite around 20:00
ticketNote: Day tickets usually around EUR 15-20.
highlights: The only night cyclocross of the season: floodlit laps through the streets and gardens of Diegem with a party atmosphere between Christmas and New Year.
tip: Arrive at dusk, stand on the steps near the church, and dress for a cold evening.
lez: Brussels low-emission zone starts just west of Diegem; park in Diegem itself.
why: Cyclocross under floodlights in a village street party, the most atmospheric cross of the winter.
dateNote: Wednesday 30 December 2026 per the published 2026-27 Belgian cyclocross calendar (Sporza); the organiser's site could not be reached from this session to confirm.

name: Het Nationale Vuurwerk Rotterdam 2026 (New Year's Eve)
times: Music from 22:30, countdown and fireworks at 00:00
venue: Erasmusbrug; best free view from the Boompjeskade
ticketNote: Free
highlights: The Netherlands' official New Year fireworks are fired from the Erasmus Bridge at midnight with a live music show broadcast on TV Rijnmond, watched by tens of thousands on the Maas quays.
tip: Stand on the Boompjeskade for the countdown, use Parkeergarage Boompjes or a P+R, and note that metro lines run until about 02:10.
parking: Parkeergarage Boompjes and five 24/7 P+R sites
train: Rotterdam Centraal, then metro to Beurs or Wilhelminaplein
lez: Rotterdam milieuzone bans older diesels in the centre
why: The national New Year fireworks over the Erasmus Bridge, a two-hour drive for the biggest midnight show in the country.
dateNote: Projected: the show is held every 31 December at the Erasmusbrug; the official site still showed the 2025/2026 edition at research time.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup Zonhoven 2027
times: Women elite early afternoon, men elite around 15:00
ticketNote: Day tickets around EUR 20-25 through the World Cup ticket shop; kids usually free.
highlights: The sand pit of De Kuil, where riders plunge down a near-vertical sand wall in front of a natural amphitheatre of fans, is the loudest venue in cyclocross.
tip: Get to the Kuil early and stand on the rim of the pit for the descent; it is 40 minutes from home so make it a Sunday afternoon.
why: The wildest sand descent in cyclocross, just across the border in Belgian Limburg.

name: Bommelsfeesten Ronse 2027
times: Sat: morning parade 10:10, evening parade 17:45, fireworks 22:00; Mon: Popverbranding 23:00
ticketNote: Free street event
highlights: Belgium's earliest carnival: the Bommels take over Ronse with a morning and an illuminated evening parade on Saturday, musical fireworks at 22:00 and the burning of the puppet on Monday night.
tip: Plan for the Saturday: watch the 17:45 evening parade from the Grote Markt and stay for the 22:00 fireworks.
why: A full carnival weekend with a lit night parade and fireworks a month before everyone else, under two hours away.

name: IHF Men's Handball World Championship 2027 (Cologne)
times: Main round from 20 Jan (throw-offs 15:30, 18:00, 20:30), quarter-finals from 26 Jan, semi-finals 29 Jan, final 31 Jan
ticketNote: Germany's main-round and knockout matchdays are sold out; tickets for non-German main-round days in Cologne were still available at the last sales phase.
highlights: Two main-round groups, all quarter-finals, both semi-finals and the final of the handball World Championship in Cologne's 19,000-seat arena, the loudest handball venue in the world.
tip: Buy a main-round day ticket for three games in a row; the Cologne arena is next to Deutz station, so take the train.
train: Köln Messe/Deutz station is beside the arena, 45 minutes from Aachen.
why: The whole knockout stage of a World Championship 75 minutes away in the loudest handball arena on earth.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup Hoogerheide 2027
times: Women elite 13:40, men elite 15:10
venue: GP Adrie van der Poel course, Scheldeweg/Onderstal
ticketNote: Tickets via the local organiser GP Adrie van der Poel.
highlights: The World Cup final on Mathieu van der Poel's home course a week before the World Championships, with the Dutch star usually riding in front of his home crowd.
tip: Arrive by noon and stand on the steep run-up near the finish; it is the last chance to see the stars before Ostend.
why: Van der Poel on home soil in the World Cup final, a week before the Worlds.

name: UCI Cyclo-cross World Championships 2027 Ostend
times: Fri: team relay 12:35; Sat: women elite 15:10; Sun: men elite 15:10
venue: Wellington Hippodrome and the beach at Thermae Palace
ticketNote: Pre-sale tickets are discounted; Sunday (men's elite) is the day that sells best.
highlights: The rainbow jerseys decided on a course that runs from the racecourse onto the North Sea beach, with Van der Poel, Van Aert and Nys on home sand in front of tens of thousands of Belgian fans.
tip: Take the train to Ostend to avoid the parking chaos and stand on the beach section where the riders dismount; Saturday has the women's elite race and smaller crowds.
train: Ostend station is a 20-minute walk from the Hippodrome; trains from Maastricht via Brussels.
why: A world championship on a Belgian beach with the Dutch and Belgian superstars fighting for the rainbow jersey.

name: Kölner Karneval 2027: Weiberfastnacht to Rosenmontagszug
times: Weiberfastnacht Thu 4 Feb from 11:11; Rosenmontagszug Mon 8 Feb (start time and route to be published)
venue: Altstadt, Heumarkt and the Rosenmontag route
ticketNote: Free along the route; grandstand seats are sold separately by the Festkomitee
highlights: Germany's largest carnival parade rolls through Cologne on Rosenmontag with over a million spectators, giant satirical floats and tons of Kamelle, after Weiberfastnacht opens the street carnival on Thursday.
tip: Arrive by train before 09:00 on Rosenmontag, pick a spot on the Severinstrasse or the Ringe rather than the Dom, and bring a bag for the sweets.
train: Trains from Heerlen or Aachen to Köln Hbf; the city centre is closed to cars on Rosenmontag
why: The Cologne Rosenmontag parade is the one carnival spectacle in Europe that matches Anne's taste for scale, just over an hour away.
dateNote: Rosenmontag 2027 falls on 8 February and Weiberfastnacht on 4 February by the carnival calendar; the Festkomitee site lists the Zug but had not yet published the 2027 start time or route at research time.

name: ABN AMRO Open 2027
times: Qualifying 6-7 Feb; day sessions from 12:00, evening sessions from 19:30; final Sun 14 Feb 13:00
ticketNote: Ground passes from EUR 17.50 (qualifying Sunday) and EUR 19.50 (Monday day session); finals weekend is the first to sell out.
highlights: The 54th edition of the ATP 500 indoor tournament, traditionally with several top-10 players and a Dutch contingent, in the Ahoy arena.
tip: A Monday or Tuesday day session gives four matches for under EUR 25; take the metro to Zuidplein.
train: Rotterdam Zuidplein metro station is a short walk from Ahoy.
why: The Netherlands' biggest tennis week, with top-10 players for the price of a cinema ticket.

name: Aalst Carnaval 2027
times: Sunday parade 13:00 from Statieplein; Monday Ajuinworp 14:30; Tuesday Voil Jeanetten 15:00, Popverbranding 21:00
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Belgium's biggest and most satirical carnival: a Sunday parade of over 5,000 participants and giant floats, the Gilles' broom dance and onion throw on Monday, and the Voil Jeanetten and puppet burning on Tuesday.
tip: Take the train (Aalst station is at the parade start) and arrive before 12:30 on Sunday for a spot near the Grote Markt where the parade ends.
train: Aalst station is next to Statieplein
why: The wildest carnival parade in Belgium is a 90-minute drive and the whole thing is free to watch.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the carnival calendar (Sunday to Tuesday before Ash Wednesday, 7-9 Feb 2027) and the 2026 programme times on aalst.be; 2027 programme not yet published.

name: Carnaval de Binche 2027
times: Mardi Gras (Tue 9 Feb) is the main day with the Gilles from early morning until the evening fireworks
ticketNote: Free street event
highlights: UNESCO-listed carnival where hundreds of Gilles in wax masks and ostrich-feather hats dance to drums, throw blood oranges into the crowd and gather for the rondeau and fireworks on the Grand-Place on Mardi Gras.
tip: Go on Mardi Gras (Tuesday), arrive before 09:00 to see the Gilles leave their houses, and never throw an orange back.
parking: Use the official car parks and shuttle buses listed on the carnival site; the centre is closed
why: One of the oldest carnivals in Europe and a UNESCO masterpiece, with a Mardi Gras the family will remember.
dateNote: Official site lists 7, 8 and 9 February 2027; Mardi Gras is 9 February.

name: Vastelaovend Maastricht 2027 (Carnival)
times: Boonte Störrem parade on Sunday 7 Feb (start time not yet published)
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Three days of street carnival in red, yellow and green, opened by the Boonte Störrem parade on Sunday and carried by the Zate Hermeniekes brass bands around the Vrijthof.
tip: Take the train from Heerlen and come in costume; the Sunday parade through the centre is the big family moment, Monday and Tuesday are for the street party.
train: Direct trains from Heerlen to Maastricht; expect crowds
why: The biggest carnival in the Netherlands is 25 minutes from home, so the family can join the Sunday parade without planning a trip.

name: Rosenmontagszug Aachen 2027
times: Parade from 11:11 (2026 pattern)
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Aachen's Rosenmontag parade winds through the old town from 11:11 with floats, bands and the Öcher Prinz; the children's parade (Kengerzoch) runs the day before on Tulpensonntag.
tip: Park at the edge of the city or take the train to Aachen Hbf and walk in; the parade starts at 11:11 so leave Hoensbroek by 10:00.
train: Aachen Hbf, 15 minutes walk to the route
why: A full German Rosenmontag parade only 30 minutes from home, so the family can see it without the Cologne crowds.
dateNote: 2027 date projected from the carnival calendar (Rosenmontag 8 Feb 2027) and the 2026 edition, which ran on Rosenmontag from 11:11; the FestAusschuss had not published 2027 details at research time.

name: Rosenmontagszug Düsseldorf 2027
times: From about 12:30
venue: Innenstadt, about 5 km route ending at Königsallee
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Jacques Tilly's famously sharp political floats lead a 5 km parade through the Düsseldorf city centre with around 600,000 spectators.
tip: Düsseldorf starts later than Cologne (around 12:30), so it suits a relaxed morning drive; stand along the Königsallee for the Tilly floats.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf, then walk to the Altstadt
why: The most political and photographed floats of German carnival, an hour away and easier to reach than Cologne on the same day.

name: Bright Brussels Festival 2027
times: Evenings, roughly 18:30-23:00 (2026 hours)
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Four evenings of light installations and projections on a free walking route through central Brussels; the 2026 edition drew 420,000 visitors.
tip: Go on the Thursday or Sunday to avoid the Saturday crush, and take the train to Brussels-Central.
train: Brussels-Central is on the route
lez: Brussels LEZ: Euro 5 diesel and older banned, register foreign cars online before entering
why: Belgium's largest light festival, free and in the carnival half-term week.
dateNote: 11-14 February 2027 announced in press and by visit.brussels partners; the official visit.brussels page still showed the 2026 edition at research time.

name: Eva Gonzalès. A New Perspective (Van Gogh Museum)
times: Daily 09:00-18:00 (check site, Fridays often later)
ticketNote: Adult €26 from 2027, under 18 free; online time-slot ticket only
highlights: First ever retrospective of the French Impressionist Eva Gonzalès (1847-1883), Manet's only pupil, with paintings and pastels on loan from international museums and private collections.
tip: Combine with the Stedelijk next door; book the Van Gogh slot first as it is the one that sells out.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then tram 2 or 12 to Van Baerlestraat
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: A world-first retrospective at the Van Gogh Museum, the most visited museum in the Netherlands, in the quieter spring months.

name: Vivian Maier: Close-up (Kunstpalast)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Thu until 21:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €17, under 18 free
highlights: More than 150 photographs by the nanny who secretly became one of the great street photographers, grouped around childhood, self-portraits, colour work and street scenes.
tip: Pair it with the free-entry Kunstpalast collection and the Escher show once it opens in March.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then tram 701 or 705 to Kunstpalast
why: The Vivian Maier story is a teenager-friendly way into photography, and the self-portraits are the best part.

name: Welcome to Paradise (Städel Frankfurt)
times: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Thu until 21:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Early-bird ticket €15 without time slot on sale now; regular timed ticket from €17, flex ticket €25
highlights: Around 80 international loans by Jan van Eyck, Robert Campin and Pisanello around the Städel's Little Garden of Paradise (c. 1410), plus a walk-in Garden of Paradise installation by Philipp Fürhofer.
tip: Buy the €15 early-bird ticket now; it has no fixed time slot so you can arrive whenever you reach Frankfurt.
train: Frankfurt Hbf, 15 minutes on foot across the Main
why: Van Eyck-level loans around one of Germany's most beloved medieval paintings, the Städel's flagship show of 2027.

name: Omloop Het Nieuwsblad 2027
venue: Start Gent, finish Ninove via the Muur van Geraardsbergen
ticketNote: Free along the route.
highlights: The opening weekend of the Belgian classics season: the first cobbles and hellingen of the year, with the Muur van Geraardsbergen and Bosberg deciding the race before the finish in Ninove.
tip: Watch the team presentation in Gent in the morning and drive to the Muur van Geraardsbergen for the decisive climb in the afternoon.
lez: Gent has a low-emission zone in the city centre; check your car's eligibility before driving in.
why: The first big classic of the year, with the Muur van Geraardsbergen back on the menu.

ticketNote: Ticket price not yet published
name: Nacht van de Militaire Muziek 2027
highlights: An evening of the Defence orchestras and bands playing among the tanks and aircraft of the National Military Museum.
tip: Buy tickets early via nmm.nl; the late-evening sets in the aircraft hall are the best.
why: Military bands playing under fighter jets, a one-night special at the national museum.

name: Luc Tuymans: Silent Music (Stedelijk)
ticketNote: Adult €22.50, included in museum entry
highlights: Nearly sixty paintings by Belgium's most influential living painter, built around the hidden forces of war, colonial memory and the uncanny in his work.
tip: Combine with the Eva Gonzalès show at the Van Gogh Museum next door on the same day.
train: Amsterdam Centraal then tram 2 or 12 to Museumplein
lez: Amsterdam milieuzone: diesel cars Euro 4 or older banned
why: A rare large survey of Luc Tuymans, worth it for anyone who follows contemporary painting.

name: The Dutch Masters (Indoor Brabant) 2027
ticketNote: Tickets via Eventim; the Sunday Rolex Grand Prix is the first session to sell out.
highlights: The Netherlands' top horse show and a leg of the Rolex Grand Slam of Show Jumping, with the world's best riders, a dressage World Cup Grand Prix and the Rolex Grand Prix on Sunday afternoon.
tip: Book Sunday for the Rolex Grand Prix and the Friday evening for the dressage freestyle.
why: A Rolex Grand Slam show, the Dutch equivalent of Aachen, 90 minutes up the A2.

train: Maastricht Randwyck station is next to the MECC
ticketNote: Tickets available from mid-November 2026: weekday €55, weekend €85, youth 12-18 €23, under 12 free
name: TEFAF Maastricht
highlights: The 40th edition of the world's leading fine art and antiques fair: leading dealers showing Old Masters, antiquities, jewellery and design, with museum curators shopping alongside you.
tip: Buy a weekday ticket for Monday to Thursday, take a free guided tour and allow a full afternoon; it is ten minutes from home so skip the parking and cycle or bus.
why: The world's greatest art fair happens ten minutes from the front door, once a year.

name: M.C. Escher and the Fascination of Seeing (Kunstpalast)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, Thu until 21:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: Adult €17, under 18 free
highlights: Over 40 Escher works from the big Dutch collections in The Hague, Arnhem and Rotterdam shown next to Bridget Riley, Gerhard Richter and Jeppe Hein, with walk-in optical installations by Christoph Niemann and Marina Apollonio.
tip: Expect school groups on weekday mornings; a Thursday evening visit avoids them.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then tram 701 or 705 to Kunstpalast
why: Escher's impossible staircases plus optical-illusion installations is the one art show the whole family will argue about.

parking: Paid parking at the garden entrance
train: Keukenhof Express bus 858 from Schiphol
ticketNote: Timed-entry tickets online only; 2027 prices not yet published; weekends and the parade weekend sell out
name: Keukenhof 2027
highlights: Millions of bulbs in flower across the gardens and pavilions, with the surrounding bulb fields in full colour from mid-April.
tip: Book a weekday morning slot in the second half of April for peak tulips and the smallest crowds, and park at the garden or take the Keukenhof Express bus from Schiphol.
why: The world's most famous spring garden is a once-a-year day out, two and a half hours away.
driveNote: Tier 1 radius exception: just over three hours

name: Olafur Eliasson (Museum Voorlinden)
ticketNote: Adult €24; time-slot tickets via the online shop
highlights: Large solo show of light, water, colour and reflection by Olafur Eliasson, centred on a 21-metre kaleidoscopic room where your reflection is fragmented and multiplied with every step.
tip: Book the first slot, walk the dune estate afterwards, and bring the teens for the mirror room.
why: Eliasson builds walk-in light spectacles, exactly the kind of immersive show this family drives for.

name: Paaspop 2027
ticketNote: Day and weekend tickets on sale since Sat 31 Oct 2026 11:00; prices on the ticket shop
highlights: The 50th anniversary edition opens the Dutch festival season with Bløf, Clouseau, De Staat, Rag'n'Bone Man, Rowwen Hèze, The Opposites, Sub Focus and a first batch of 50 names.
tip: Saturday sells out first every year; buy a day ticket now and drive, it is about an hour up the A2/A50.
why: The first big festival of the year and a special 50th edition, close enough for a day trip.

name: Gent-Wevelgem In Flanders Fields 2027
venue: Start Middelkerke, finish Wevelgem via the Kemmelberg
ticketNote: Free along the route.
highlights: The sprinters' classic crosses the Flanders Fields battlefields, the Plugstreets gravel and the cobbled Kemmelberg before a fast finish in Wevelgem; the women's race runs the same day.
tip: Stand on the Kemmelberg for the decisive climb and combine the day with the Menin Gate in Ypres, 15 minutes away.
why: A cobbled classic through the First World War battlefields that Nick will want to see.

name: Ronde van Vlaanderen 2027
times: We Ride Flanders sportive Sat 3 Apr; women's and men's races Sun 4 Apr with finishes in Oudenaarde
venue: Finish Oudenaarde, climbs Oude Kwaremont and Paterberg
ticketNote: Free along the route; paid VIP villages on the Oude Kwaremont and Paterberg.
highlights: Flanders' Finest, the cobbled Monument that is a national holiday in Belgium: the Oude Kwaremont and Paterberg are climbed three times in front of beer-fuelled crowds before the finish in Oudenaarde.
tip: Base yourself in Kwaremont village, which sees the race pass three times with big screens and food stalls, and arrive before 11:00 because roads close.
why: The most atmospheric day in cycling, with cobbled climbs you can stand on for free.

ticketNote: Price for the 11th edition not yet published
name: Museumnacht Maastricht
highlights: The 11th Museumnacht opens Maastricht's museums, galleries and heritage sites for one Friday night with music, performances and tours.
tip: Start at the Bonnefanten or Centre Céramique and walk the Wyck-to-centre route; it is ten minutes from home so go late.
why: Maastricht's museums after dark, with music and performances, a short drive from home.

name: NN Marathon Rotterdam 2027
times: Kids and short-distance runs Sat 10 Apr; marathon Sun 11 Apr from 10:00
venue: Start and finish on the Coolsingel, Erasmus Bridge crossing
ticketNote: Free to watch; entry to run sells out quickly.
highlights: The Netherlands' biggest marathon with hundreds of thousands of spectators, the famous crossing of the Erasmus Bridge and the finish on the Coolsingel.
tip: Watch the elite start on the Coolsingel at 10:00, walk to the Erasmus Bridge for the first crossing, and be back at the finish around 12:05 for the winner.
why: The country's biggest marathon party, free on the streets of Rotterdam.

name: Premier League Darts 2027 Rotterdam
times: Evening, doors around 17:30, play from 18:00 (Rotterdam night starts earlier than usual)
ticketNote: Sells out within days of going on sale; tickets through Ahoy and Ticketmaster only.
highlights: The Dutch night of the Premier League with Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gian van Veen in front of 10,000 fancy-dressed fans in Ahoy.
tip: Set an alert for the on-sale date and dress up; the walk-ons and the crowd are half the show for a 14-year-old.
train: Rotterdam Zuidplein metro station next to Ahoy.
why: Littler and Van Gerwen in the loudest darts crowd in the world, 90 minutes away.
dateNote: Thursday 15 April 2027 per the PDC's 2027 Premier League schedule as reported by Sky Sports and others on 25 September 2026; the pdc.tv page could not be read from this session.

times: Fri 14:00 to Sun 20:00
ticketNote: Early Bird: Friday €30, Saturday €46, Sunday €34, 3-day €72; children 7-12 reduced, under 7 free
name: AnimeCon
highlights: The Netherlands' biggest anime convention: cosplay competitions, J-pop and K-pop performances, dealer room, gaming and 24-hour programming.
tip: Saturday is the main day; buy early-bird tickets now and take the train to Rijswijk station (10-minute walk).
why: The main Dutch anime weekend, with K-pop and cosplay stages, a fan event made for Alma.

name: Amstel Gold Race 2027
times: Toertocht Sat 17 Apr; women's and men's pro races Sun 18 Apr, finish mid-afternoon in Valkenburg
ticketNote: Free along the roadside; VIP packages on the Cauberg are the only paid option.
highlights: The Netherlands' only WorldTour classic loops through the Limburg hills for the whole day, with the women's and men's pelotons passing the Cauberg several times and finishing in Valkenburg.
tip: Cycle or walk to the Cauberg or the Bemelerberg, pick a spot the peloton passes three times, and bring a radio for the live commentary; the finish area in Valkenburg fills by noon.
why: The biggest sporting day in Limburg rolls past the front door for free.

dateNote: The 80th parade drives on Saturday 17 April 2027; the official 'Corso 2027' programme runs 14-18 April with float-building days and an illuminated parade in Noordwijkerhout on the Friday evening.
ticketNote: Free along the route; grandstand seats in some towns are ticketed
name: Bloemencorso Bollenstreek
highlights: Giant floats and decorated cars covered in hyacinths, tulips and daffodils drive 42 km from Noordwijk through Lisse past Keukenhof to Haarlem.
tip: Pick Lisse (the floats pass Keukenhof around midday) and combine it with a Keukenhof visit, but book Keukenhof timed tickets early as this weekend sells out.
why: The largest flower parade in the Netherlands, rolling past Keukenhof at the peak of tulip season.
driveNote: Tier 1 radius exception: just over three hours

name: c/o pop Festival 2027
ticketNote: Festival passes via infield.live; prices not yet listed
highlights: Five days of new pop, indie and electronic acts in the clubs, halls and streets of Cologne's Ehrenfeld district, with free open-air stages.
tip: Go on the Saturday for the free outdoor programme in Ehrenfeld and the Venloer Strasse street scene.
train: Köln-Ehrenfeld S-Bahn
why: A city showcase festival for discovering next year's headliners an hour away in Cologne.

name: La Flèche Wallonne 2027
times: Women's and men's finishes on the Mur de Huy in the afternoon
venue: Finish on the Mur de Huy
ticketNote: Free on the Mur de Huy.
highlights: A midweek classic that climbs the brutal Mur de Huy three times and finishes on its 26 percent ramp; the women's race finishes there the same afternoon.
tip: Be on the Mur by midday to get a spot on the steepest bend and see both the women's and the men's finish.
why: The steepest finish in classic cycling, an hour from home on a Wednesday afternoon.

times: Dawn service 06:00 at Buttes New British Cemetery; Tyne Cot 09:30; Menin Gate 11:00 (2026 pattern)
venue: Buttes New British Cemetery, Polygon Wood; Tyne Cot; Menin Gate
ticketNote: Free
dateNote: 25 April is fixed; 2027 times projected from the 2026 programme.
name: Anzac Day Dawn Service, Polygon Wood and Menin Gate 2027
highlights: Australian and New Zealand dawn service among the trees of Polygon Wood, organised with the Passchendaele Museum, then services at Tyne Cot and a special Last Post at the Menin Gate.
tip: Park at the Passchendaele Museum by 05:00 for the shuttle; roads around Polygon Wood are closed.
why: A dawn service in a WWI wood is a rare, atmospheric commemoration for a military professional.

name: Liège-Bastogne-Liège 2027
times: Start around 10:00 in Liège, finish about 17:00 in Liège
venue: Start and finish Liège, via the Ardennes
ticketNote: Free along the route; official VIP hospitality only at the finish.
highlights: La Doyenne, the oldest of cycling's five Monuments, climbs La Redoute and the Roche-aux-Faucons before finishing on the Quai des Ardennes in Liège; the women's race runs the same day.
tip: Drive to La Redoute (Remouchamps) by 13:00 for the loudest atmosphere, or stand at the finish in Liège, 40 minutes from home.
why: A cycling Monument that finishes 40 minutes from home, with the Ardennes climbs as a stage.

ticketNote: Free
name: Koningsdag 2027 with the Royal Family
highlights: King Willem-Alexander celebrates his 60th birthday with Queen Máxima, the three princesses and the wider royal family on a walking route through Lelystad, the first King's Day ever held in Flevoland.
tip: The royal route and programme are published by the city in the weeks before; arrive early by train as the centre closes to cars, and expect security checks along the route.
why: See the whole royal family at close range on the King's milestone 60th birthday.
driveNote: Tier 1 radius exception: just over three hours

name: Eschborn-Frankfurt 2027
venue: Finish at the Alte Oper, Frankfurt
ticketNote: Free; the ADAC Velotour sportive the same morning requires registration.
highlights: Germany's only WorldTour one-day race, held on the 1 May holiday, climbs the Taunus hills before a sprint finish in front of the Alte Oper with tens of thousands of spectators.
tip: Watch the Mammolshainer climb at midday and then take the S-Bahn into the city for the finish on the Opernplatz.
lez: Frankfurt has an Umweltzone; a green sticker is required for the city centre.
why: Germany's biggest road race, a May Day out in Frankfurt with a city-centre finish.
dateNote: The organiser's site shows 1 May 2027; the UCI calendar initially listed 2 May but the organiser has stated the race stays on 1 May.

name: Rhein in Flammen Bonn 2027
times: Festival in the Rheinaue from the afternoon, fireworks late evening
venue: Rheinaue park and the Rhine between Bonn and Königswinter
ticketNote: Free from the Rheinaue park; ship places sold by the shipping companies
highlights: The first Rhein in Flammen of the year: an illuminated ship convoy sails from Linz past Königswinter to Bonn, where a big musical fireworks show closes a day-long festival in the Rheinaue park.
tip: Set up on the Rheinaue lawns early with a picnic, or watch from the Königswinter bank where the convoy passes before Bonn.
train: Bonn Hbf then tram to Rheinaue; or Königswinter station for the Siebengebirge bank
why: Fireworks over the Rhine and the Siebengebirge, about 90 minutes from home and free.
dateNote: 2027 date projected from the first-Saturday-of-May pattern (2 May 2026 on the official site); Bonn 2027 was not yet listed while the other 2027 Rhein in Flammen dates were.

name: Ruhrfestspiele Recklinghausen 2027
ticketNote: Programme published early March 2027; presale start to be announced
highlights: One of Europe's oldest theatre festivals, six weeks of international drama, dance and circus opening with the 1 May 'Kulturvolksfest' in the Stadtgarten.
tip: The 1 May opening day is a big free open-air family fair around the Festspielhaus; book the international productions when the programme drops in March.
why: A major international theatre festival with a free 1 May family fair about 90 minutes away.
dateNote: Official site states '1 May to mid-June 2027'; end date 13 June projected (2026 ran 1 May to 13 June).

times: Ceremony from about 19:45; two minutes' silence 20:00
ticketNote: Free, no registration
name: Nationale Herdenking op de Dam 2027
highlights: The national remembrance with the King and Queen laying the first wreath at the National Monument, two minutes of silence across the country, the Wilhelmus and wreaths from veterans and survivors, broadcast live.
tip: Be on the Dam by 18:30 to get a standing place; shops close at 19:00 and the city falls silent.
why: The Netherlands' national remembrance ceremony, in person on the Dam, is unforgettable once.

ticketNote: Free
dateNote: Always 5 May at the Arloterrein in Roermond; 2027 line-up not yet announced.
name: Bevrijdingsfestival Limburg 2027
highlights: Limburg's official Liberation Day festival: two music stages with national headliners and the Ambassadors of Freedom arriving by helicopter, a Plein van de Vrijheid with veterans and Defence stands, a Freedom Meal and children's programme.
tip: Go early afternoon for the Ambassador of Freedom helicopter landing and the Defence displays before the evening crowds.
why: Limburg's own free Liberation Day festival, 30 minutes from home, with live bands for everyone.

times: National capitulation commemoration around midday, defilé from early afternoon (2025 pattern: 12:30)
venue: 5 Mei Plein and Hotel De Wereld
ticketNote: Free
dateNote: Fixed on 5 May each year; the 2027 programme will be published in spring 2027.
name: Vrijheidsdefilé Wageningen 2027 (Liberation Day parade)
highlights: The Liberation Day parade past Hotel De Wereld, where the German capitulation was signed, led by WWII veterans and followed by 2,500 serving soldiers from allied nations, military bands and historic vehicles, with the Bevrijdingsfestival Gelderland around it.
tip: Claim a spot on the Gen. Foulkesweg before 12:00 and stay for the free festival stages.
why: The Netherlands' liberation parade, with allied and even German troops marching past the veterans, on the day itself.

name: Heilig Bloedprocessie Brugge 2027
times: Procession 14:30; closing celebration on the Burg 17:30
venue: Historic centre, starting from the Burg
ticketNote: Free standing along the route; grandstand seats sold via the procession website
highlights: On Ascension Day some 1,700 participants in biblical and medieval costume, with floats, animals and the relic of the Holy Blood, parade through Bruges in a UNESCO-listed procession dating back to 1304.
tip: Book grandstand seats early or claim a spot on the Markt by 13:30; the relic transfer at 10:30 and the closing at 17:30 on the Burg bookend the day.
train: Brugge station, 15 minutes walk to the Markt
why: A once-a-year UNESCO pageant through the best-preserved medieval city in Belgium, on a public holiday.

name: Kattenstoet Ieper 2027
times: Afternoon parade, followed by the cat throwing from the Belfry and the witch burning
ticketNote: Free standing; grandstand seats sold in advance
highlights: Once every three years Ieper stages a 2,000-strong cat-themed parade with giants, floats and brass bands, ending with the jester throwing plush cats from the Belfry and a mock witch burning on the Grote Markt.
tip: Arrive before noon, park outside the ramparts, and stand near the Belfry for the cat throwing at the end.
why: A triennial parade that will not come back until 2030, with giants and flying plush cats that Alma will love.
dateNote: Projected: the Kattenstoet is held every three years on the second Sunday of May (last edition 12 May 2024), which gives 9 May 2027; the official site was unreachable at research time, confirm before travelling.

train: Westerpark is a 15-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal
dateNote: I amsterdam lists 12-16 May 2027 (Ascension weekend) with the note that 2027 dates and times are subject to change.
ticketNote: Free entry; debit card only at the kitchens
name: Het Weekend van de Rollende Keukens
highlights: The Netherlands' biggest food-truck festival fills the Westerpark with dozens of mobile kitchens, live music and a buy-and-keep festival glass.
tip: Do not come by car; take the train to Amsterdam Centraal and walk or take bus 21, and go on a weekday afternoon for shorter queues.
why: Street food from every corner of the world in one park, timed for the Ascension long weekend.

name: FIA WEC TotalEnergies 6 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps 2027
times: Race on Saturday 15 May
ticketNote: General admission and grandstand tickets through the FIA WEC ticket shop; usually under EUR 60 for the weekend.
highlights: The Hypercars of Ferrari, Porsche, Toyota, BMW and Cadillac in their last big test before Le Mans, racing six hours around Spa on the Saturday.
tip: Watch from the inside of Les Combes for the best overtaking, and walk the pit lane during the Friday pit walk.
why: The Le Mans Hypercars race on the Ardennes rollercoaster an hour from home.

name: Extrema Outdoor Belgium 2027
ticketNote: Line-up drops and ticket sale to be announced
highlights: Three days of house and techno on the lake at De Plas, with elaborate stage design and a Sunday closing on the beach.
tip: Sunday on the beach stage is the relaxed day; it is 45 minutes from home so skip the camping.
why: Belgian Limburg's biggest electronic festival on a lake, an easy day trip for Anne.

name: IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship 2027 (Düsseldorf)
times: Group games daily, mostly 16:20 and 20:20; semi-finals and final in Düsseldorf on 29-30 May
venue: PSD Bank Dome, Düsseldorf (co-host Mannheim SAP Arena)
ticketNote: Day tickets and venue packages via the DEB shop; all tickets include public transport. The opening game Germany v Switzerland on 13 May at Veltins-Arena Gelsenkirchen (38,000 seats) sold out within hours.
highlights: The men's ice hockey World Championship in Germany for the first time since 2017, with the group games and the entire final weekend (semi-finals, bronze and gold games) in Düsseldorf's new arena.
tip: Pick a group day with two games for the price of one and take the U-Bahn to the arena on your ticket; final-weekend seats will be the first to go.
train: Event tickets include VRR public transport; the arena has its own U78 stop.
why: A world championship final weekend 80 minutes away, with two games a day for one ticket.

ticketNote: Free entry; a Tasting Pass with glass and VRM transport ticket can be bought in advance
name: Weinmarkt der Ahr
highlights: Whitsun wine market of the Ahr valley's red-wine estates on the medieval market square inside Ahrweiler's town walls, organised by Ahrwein e.V.
tip: Buy the Tasting Pass that includes the VRM public-transport ticket and take the Ahrtalbahn so nobody has to drive.
why: Germany's red-wine valley, rebuilt after the 2021 flood, celebrates in a walled medieval town ninety minutes away.

name: Militracks 2027

why: Anime and K-pop fandom on a huge scale, one hour from home, and it sells out fast.

name: NN North Sea Jazz Festival 2027
ticketNote: Day tickets usually go on sale in February after the first names; no 2027 prices yet
highlights: The world's largest indoor jazz festival with around 150 acts across 13 Ahoy stages, from jazz legends to soul and pop crossover headliners.
tip: Pick the day with the biggest crossover headliner and arrive early for the Maas hall sets, which fill up fast.
train: Rotterdam Zuidplein metro, next to Ahoy
why: A world-renowned festival where one day ticket gets you 50 concerts under one roof.

name: Fêtes de Gayant Douai 2027
times: Giants' processions on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday; main cortège on Sunday
venue: Place d'Armes and old town of Douai
ticketNote: Free
highlights: The giant Gayant family (8.5 m tall Monsieur Gayant, his wife and three children) is carried through Douai for three days with bands, folk groups and the Sot des Canonniers, a UNESCO-listed giants tradition since 1530.
tip: Go on the Sunday for the main cortège and stand on the Place d'Armes where the giants dance.
why: One of the great giant processions of northern France and a UNESCO tradition, about 2.5 hours from home.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed rule (Sunday after 5 July plus the two following days; 2026 edition ran 12-14 July); official programme not yet published.

name: Francofolies de Spa 2027
venue: Spa town centre (Pierre Rapsat stage and Village)

highlights: Three days of French-language pop, chanson and rap in the spa town's streets and park, with free Village stages beside the ticketed main stage.

why: A charming francophone pop festival an hour away with lots of free street stages for the family.
dateNote: Dates 16-18 July 2027 (open-air formula) come from the festival's 25 Sep 2026 newsletter as reported by info-lux.com on 3 Oct 2026; the official site could not be read directly.

name: Gentse Feesten 2027
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Ten days of free concerts, street theatre, parades and fireworks on a dozen squares in the medieval centre, one of Europe's biggest city festivals.

why: Europe's largest free city festival turns the whole of Ghent into a stage for ten days, about two hours away.

name: Parookaville 2027
ticketNote: Ticket shop open now, day tickets available; prices on the official shop
highlights: Germany's biggest EDM festival builds a fantasy city on Weeze airport with Lost Frequencies, Steve Aoki, Don Diablo and BUNT. already confirmed.
tip: Day tickets are the family option; the Mainstage closing show with fireworks is the moment to stay for.
why: A Tomorrowland-style city of stages and fireworks just an hour north, with day tickets that make it doable without camping.

name: Rheinkirmes Düsseldorf 2027 (Grösste Kirmes am Rhein)
times: Fireworks Fri 23 Jul about 22:30; drone shows Tue 20 and Fri 23 Jul about 22:15
ticketNote: Free entry, pay per ride
highlights: The biggest funfair on the Rhine covers 165,000 square metres of the Oberkassel meadows opposite the Altstadt, with giant rides, beer tents, a drone show and a large fireworks display on the final Friday.
tip: Pick the final Friday (23 July) for the fireworks and watch them from the Altstadt bank or the Rheinkniebrücke if you want to skip the crowds on the fairground.
train: U-Bahn to Luegplatz or Belsenplatz (Oberkassel)
why: A giant fair plus Rhine fireworks and a drone show, an hour from home.
dateNote: visitduesseldorf.de body text gives 16-25 July 2027 (the page header says 16-27, a typo: the fair always runs Friday to Sunday over 10 days).

name: Tilburgse Kermis 2027
times: Daily from early afternoon until late
ticketNote: Free entry, pay per ride
highlights: The largest funfair in the Benelux spreads over 200 attractions through the streets of Tilburg for ten days, with Roze Maandag (Pink Monday) as its famous party day.
tip: Go on a weekday afternoon for shorter queues on the big rides, and take the train as the centre is closed to cars.
train: Tilburg station is at the edge of the fair
why: The biggest street funfair in the Benelux is a 90-minute drive and a full day out for Alma.

name: Tomorrowland 2027
ticketNote: Pre-registration usually opens in early December, worldwide sale in late January; day passes sell out within hours
highlights: The world's most spectacular dance festival with 15 themed stages, daily fireworks and the famous Mainstage show over two weekends in De Schorre park.
tip: Pre-register on tomorrowland.com the moment registration opens and have the whole family queue for the sale; Global Journey packages are the realistic route for latecomers.
why: Nothing else in Europe matches the stage design and pyrotechnics of Tomorrowland, and it is only an hour and a half from home.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the festival's fixed pattern (third and fourth weekends of July: 17-19 and 24-26 July 2026, 18-20 and 25-27 July 2025); official site could not be fetched and has not announced 2027 dates as of 4 Nov 2026.

train: Nijmegen station is in the festival zone
ticketNote: Free; optional €12.50 wristband for toilets and an extra daily programme
name: Vierdaagsefeesten Nijmegen
highlights: The Netherlands' largest free festival: seven days of stages, street theatre and fireworks across Nijmegen around the Four Days Marches, ending with the walkers' triumphant entry on the Via Gladiola on Friday.
tip: Go on the Friday to see the walkers finish on the Via Gladiola, and take the train because the centre is closed to cars.
why: A city-wide free party with fireworks and the emotional finish of the world's largest walking event.

times: Walkers start 04:00-07:00 daily; Via Gladiola finish Friday from early afternoon
venue: Start/finish at De Wedren; Vierdaagsefeesten in the city centre
ticketNote: Free to watch; walker registration opens in early 2027 and is oversubscribed
train: Nijmegen station is a short walk from the Via Gladiola
name: Nijmeegse Vierdaagse 2027 (109th Four Days Marches)
highlights: The world's largest multi-day walking event with 45,000 walkers, thousands of them military teams from NATO nations marching in uniform with packs, ending with the gladiolus-lined Via Gladiola finish on Friday and a week-long city festival.
tip: Watch the military detachments march in on the Via Gladiola on Friday afternoon, or register early if Nick wants to walk with a JFC team.
why: Thousands of allied soldiers march the Vierdaagse every year and the Friday finish is a national celebration.

venue: Place des Palais, Parc de Bruxelles and Cinquantenaire
ticketNote: Free

lez: Brussels LEZ applies to the whole region; check your car is allowed or take the train
dateNote: 21 July is fixed; the 2027 programme and times are projected from the 2026 edition.
name: Belgian National Day Parade and Fireworks, Brussels 2027
highlights: The King takes the salute at the parade of Belgian and allied troops, armour and a flypast on the Place des Palais, after a day of military and police villages, demonstrations and concerts in the park, ending with a concert and a fireworks, laser and drone show at the Cinquantenaire.
tip: Take the train to Brussels-Central, arrive by 14:30 for a barrier spot on Rue Royale, then walk to the Cinquantenaire for the fireworks.
why: Belgium's biggest military parade plus a drone and fireworks finale in one free day, under two hours away.

name: Formula 1 Belgian Grand Prix 2027
times: Practice Fri 23 Jul, qualifying Sat 24 Jul, race Sun 25 Jul (times TBC)
ticketNote: Spa alternates with Barcelona from 2027, so this is the only Belgian GP until 2029; Bronze general admission is the cheapest category, prices for 2027 not yet published.

parking: Official car parks around the circuit are sold as separate tickets; shuttle buses run from Spa and Stavelot.
why: The world's greatest Grand Prix circuit is on our doorstep and 2027 is the only Belgian GP for two years.

name: Foire de Libramont 2027
times: Daytime, four days
venue: Libramont Exhibition and Congress fairground, Rue des Aubépines 50
ticketNote: Paid entry; 2027 prices not yet published
highlights: Europe's largest open-air agricultural fair: 200,000 visitors, thousands of animals, horse and cattle shows, forestry and giant machinery demonstrations and a full programme of equestrian shows.
tip: Arrive at opening, use the signposted car parks and shuttles, and plan the horse-show ring and the machinery field as your two anchors.
why: A huge once-a-year fair with animals, horses and monster machinery, 90 minutes away in the Ardennes.

name: Solar Weekend Festival 2027
ticketNote: Camping already sold out; weekend and day tickets go on sale later
highlights: Four days of dance, hip-hop and pop on the Maasplassen lakes with a beach, art installations and a fireworks finale.
tip: Day tickets are the way in for a family since the camping is gone; it is 30 minutes from home.
why: Limburg's own big beach festival half an hour away, with day tickets for a teenager and her parents.

name: Juicy Beats 2027
ticketNote: Early bird was 95 EUR until 30 Sep 2026; current weekend price on the ticket shop
highlights: A two-day pop, rap and electronic festival in Dortmund's Westfalenpark headlined by FiNCH and Trailerpark.
tip: The park setting is relaxed and the Florianturm is open; take the U-Bahn to Westfalenpark rather than driving into the city.
why: A pleasant park festival with German pop and rap headliners within 90 minutes of home.

name: Kölner Lichter 2027
times: Ship convoy and stage programme from the evening, fireworks late (around 23:00 in past years)
venue: Rhine between Zoobrücke and Deutzer Brücke, Altstadt and Tanzbrunnen banks
ticketNote: Free from the Rhine banks; ship, grandstand, Riesenrad and cable-car packages sold by the organiser (presale open)
highlights: Germany's largest musical fireworks show lights up the Rhine in front of Cologne Cathedral after an illuminated convoy of some 50 ships and a drone show, watched by hundreds of thousands on both banks.
tip: Arrive by late afternoon with a picnic for a free spot on the Deutz bank facing the Dom, or book the Rheinterrassen or a ship early for a guaranteed view.
train: Köln Hbf or Köln Messe/Deutz; extra trains run after midnight
why: The biggest fireworks show in Germany, in front of the cathedral, just over an hour from home.
dateNote: Official site lists the 22nd edition for 31 July 2027, marked 'in Planung'; the 2026 show was delayed and started around 23:20.

name: Cranger Kirmes Herne 2027
times: Thu 5 Aug 14:00-24:00; Fri/Sat until 02:00; fireworks Fri 6 Aug and Sun 15 Aug 22:30; parade Sat 7 Aug 10:30
venue: Cranger Kirmesplatz, main entrance Cranger Tor (Dorstener Strasse)
ticketNote: Free entry, pay per ride; Wednesday 11 Aug is family discount day
highlights: Germany's biggest funfair after the Oktoberfest, with over 500 showmen, the largest travelling rides, a Saturday parade and two fireworks nights on the opening Friday and the closing Sunday.
tip: Use the park-and-ride at A42 exit Herne-Baukau, and go on the opening Friday or the closing Sunday for the 22:30 fireworks; Wednesday is cheapest for the rides.
parking: P+R with shuttle buses from A42 exit Herne-Baukau; driving to the site is discouraged
train: Wanne-Eickel Hbf or Herne, then special buses
why: The largest funfair in north-west Germany with two fireworks nights, about 90 minutes away.

name: Theaterfestival Boulevard 2027
venue: Parade (at the foot of the Sint-Jan) and locations across the city
ticketNote: A large part of the programme is free; paid shows ticketed per performance, programme published in June
highlights: Eleven days of theatre, circus, dance and street spectacle on the Parade square and in surprising outdoor locations around Den Bosch.
tip: Pick an evening with a big outdoor spectacle on the Parade and eat at the festival square; most free shows need no booking.
train: 's-Hertogenbosch station, 15 minutes on foot
why: The biggest summer theatre festival in the south with lots of free open-air spectacle for Anne and the kids.

name: Ronquières Festival 2027
ticketNote: Tickets via Paylogic; prices and line-up to be announced
highlights: A three-day pop and rock festival at the foot of the giant Ronquières inclined boat lift, with French and international headliners.
tip: The site under the canal lift is spectacular at sunset; it is just under two hours, so plan one day.
why: A big Walloon pop festival in the unique setting of the Ronquières boat lift.

train: Amsterdam Centraal, then walk; the centre is closed to traffic
dateNote: Pride Amsterdam 2027 runs 31 July to 8 August; the Canal Parade sails on Saturday 7 August 2027.
ticketNote: Free along the canals
name: Pride Amsterdam Canal Parade
highlights: Dozens of decorated boats sail the Prinsengracht and Amstel in the world's best-known Pride parade on water, with huge crowds lining the quays.
tip: Claim a spot on the Prinsengracht by 11:00 (the parade starts around 12:30) or book a canal-side terrace months ahead, and come by train.
why: A parade of boats through the canals is the single most spectacular free event in the Dutch summer.

name: Meyboom Brussels 2027
times: Planting at 13:00; giants and entertainment on the Grand-Place from 14:00
venue: Corner of Rue des Sables and Rue du Marais, then Grand-Place
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Every 9 August since 1308 the Companions of Saint-Laurent carry the Meyboom tree through central Brussels with giants and brass bands and plant it before 17:00, a tradition on the UNESCO list of giants and dragons processions.
tip: Be at Rue des Sables before 13:00 for the planting, then follow the giants to the Grand-Place.
train: Brussels-Central, 10 minutes walk
lez: Brussels LEZ: register foreign cars online before entering
why: A 700-year-old giants parade in central Brussels on a summer Monday, worth adding to a Brussels day out.
dateNote: Meyboom calendar page lists Monday 9 August at 13:00, which matches 2027 (9 August 2027 is a Monday).

name: BELMOT Oldtimer-Grand-Prix Nürburgring 2027
ticketNote: Day and weekend tickets usually from around EUR 20-40 with free paddock access.
highlights: Germany's largest historic motorsport festival: historic Formula 1, 1960s GTs, touring cars and pre-war Grand Prix cars racing, plus thousands of classic cars in the car parks. The 2027 edition falls in the circuit's centenary year.
tip: Wander the open paddock in the morning and watch the historic F1 grid from the Mercedes tribune in the afternoon.
why: A century of racing cars driven in anger at the Nürburgring in its 100th birthday year.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the mid-August pattern and a third-party listing of 13-15 August 2027; the organiser's contract runs to 2028 but nuerburgring.de has not yet published the 2027 dates.

ticketNote: Free entry
name: Rheingauer Weinwoche
highlights: The 50th anniversary edition: around 120 stands from Rheingau estates pour almost 1,000 Rieslings and Sekts for ten days in front of Wiesbaden's palace and town hall.
tip: Take the train to Wiesbaden Hauptbahnhof and walk ten minutes; weekday evenings are far calmer than the weekends.
why: The world's largest wine festival for a single grape region celebrates its 50th birthday in 2027.

name: Ruhrtriennale 2027
venue: Jahrhunderthalle Bochum and industrial monuments across the Ruhr
ticketNote: Programme and presale start for 2027 to be announced by newsletter (usually spring)

tip: Pick one big music-theatre production in the Jahrhunderthalle Bochum and combine it with the Zollverein or Landschaftspark Duisburg.
why: World-class avant-garde opera and theatre inside monumental industrial halls, a signature Ruhr experience for Nick and Anne.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the usual mid-August to late-September window (2025: 21 Aug to 21 Sep); official site has not published them.

name: Rhein in Flammen Koblenz 2027

train: Koblenz Hbf, 20 minutes walk to the Rhine
why: The biggest fireworks show on the Rhine, best seen from the Koblenz bank at the Deutsches Eck.

why: A WorldTour stage race that often rolls through Limburg in the summer holidays.

why: The closest big festival after Pinkpop and the one with the most pop and hip-hop for a 14-year-old.

why: A fireworks competition on the beach that makes a great end to a seaside weekend in August.

highlights: Three days of music, theatre, comedy, science and art on the Walibi grounds, the Netherlands' most complete festival weekend.

why: Lowlands is the one Dutch festival worth a full camping weekend, with far more than music on the bill.

name: Schueberfouer Luxembourg 2027

why: A giant historic funfair in Luxembourg City, 90 minutes away and easy with free public transport.

why: The most famous giants procession in Belgium and a UNESCO masterpiece, two hours from home.

why: The only day of the year to eat mussels on the quay where they are landed and sail out to the mussel beds.

why: The biggest gaming show on the planet is an hour from home and the first thing Alma would ask for.

name: Ballonfiësta Barneveld 2027

why: Forty balloons at golden hour and a music-and-laser Nightglow make this the most spectacular balloon evening in the Netherlands.

name: Mainzer Weinmarkt
highlights: Rheinhessen's winemakers pour under the old trees of the Mainz Stadtpark over two long weekends, with food stalls and a fairground for kids.
tip: Come on the Thursday or Sunday for space at the tables, and park at the Volkspark or take the tram from Mainz Hauptbahnhof.
why: One of Germany's most atmospheric wine festivals, in a riverside park rather than a tent city.

train: Maastricht station is a 15-minute walk from the Vrijthof
ticketNote: Free entry; you buy 'preuvenelappen' coupons to pay at the stands
name: 't Preuvenemint Maastricht
highlights: Dozens of Limburg restaurants turn the Vrijthof into one giant open-air restaurant for four days, with live music on stage every evening.
tip: Go on Thursday or Sunday afternoon to avoid the Friday and Saturday evening crush, and buy coupons at the central kassa before you queue at a stand.
why: The biggest culinary festival in Limburg sits twenty minutes from home and costs nothing to enter.

name: Zomerparkfeest Venlo 2027

highlights: Four days of Dutch pop, hip-hop and electronic acts, theatre and food in Venlo's Julianapark, with free club nights at Grenswerk afterwards.
tip: Come by train to Venlo station and walk; the park gets crowded on Saturday evening so arrive before the headliner.
train: Venlo station, 10 minutes on foot
why: A relaxed, free city park festival 45 minutes up the A73 that suits a family evening out.

name: Cultura Nova 2027
venue: Parkstad Limburg Theaters and outdoor locations across Parkstad
ticketNote: Many outdoor spectacles free; ticketed shows via Parkstad Limburg Theaters (plt.nl), box office Burg. van Grunsvenplein 145
highlights: Ten days of international street theatre, circus, dance and large outdoor spectacle in Heerlen and Parkstad, with giant inflatables (Plasticiens Volants) and circus companies in recent years.
tip: Watch for the big free opening and closing spectacles in Heerlen centre; it is five minutes from home so go several evenings.
why: The home-town festival of outdoor spectacle, with free giant shows a five-minute drive away.

name: Mysteryland 2027

highlights: The world's oldest dance festival returns after a year off with a new concept, three days of stages, art and decor at its Haarlemmermeer home.
tip: Join the Loyalty Sale waitlist now; the relaunch edition will be in high demand.
why: A legendary dance festival relaunching in a new form, a two-hour trip for Anne.
