ticketNote: Museum admission applies; price not yet published
name: Soesterberg Zomeroffensief 2027
highlights: The museum's big outdoor weekend on the old air base: driving tanks and armoured vehicles, helicopter and aircraft displays, re-enactor camps and demonstrations by serving units.
tip: Arrive at opening and head to the outdoor arena first for the armour demonstrations.
why: Running tanks and flying displays at the national military museum, a proper family day out.

name: Weinfest der Mittelmosel
highlights: The Mosel's biggest wine festival: a 300-metre wine street on the riverbank, the crowning of the Mosel wine queen, a big fireworks show over the river on Saturday night and a parade through the old town on Sunday afternoon.
tip: Watch the Saturday fireworks from the Kues bank opposite the old town, and arrive before 14:00 on Sunday for a spot on the parade route over the Mosel bridge.
why: Fireworks over the Mosel and a parade through one of Germany's prettiest half-timbered towns, two hours from home.

ticketNote: Free entry; you pay per tasting with tokens
name: Belgian Beer Weekend
highlights: More than 50 Belgian breweries pour hundreds of beers on the UNESCO-listed Grand-Place, opened by a brewers' procession and the blessing of the beer.
tip: Arrive Friday evening or early Saturday before the square fills, and take the train: Brussels-Central is a five-minute walk.
why: Belgium's beer culture, itself on the UNESCO intangible heritage list, celebrated on the most beautiful square in Europe.

name: Vredefeesten Sint-Niklaas 2027 (balloon festival on the Grote Markt)
times: Balloon launches in the early evening and at dawn, weather permitting
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Dozens of hot-air balloons, including vintage and special shapes, inflate and launch from the largest market square in Belgium, surrounded by free concerts, street animation and the Ballonloop run in the Stadspark.
tip: Be on the Grote Markt by 18:00 for the evening launch and check the organisers' social media the same afternoon, because launches are cancelled when it is too windy.
train: Sint-Niklaas station is a 10-minute walk from the Grote Markt.
why: Nowhere else in Europe do this many balloons take off from a city square, and the whole weekend is free.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the annual pattern (first weekend of September: 4-6 Sep 2026, 5-7 Sep 2025); the official site only says 'tot volgend jaar'. Expect Fri 3 to Sun 5 September 2027.

times: Mass balloon launches mornings and early evenings; Night Glows on the Friday and Saturday evenings
venue: Montgolfiade grounds at the Warsteiner brewery, Warstein
ticketNote: Entry prices for 2027 not yet published; the grounds have a festival tent, fairground and camping.
highlights: Nine days of mass launches with up to 200 balloons, one of the largest balloon festivals in Europe, with Night Glows, a festival tent with concerts and a fairground.
tip: Go on one of the two weekends for the Night Glow, arrive early in the afternoon for parking, and check the morning launch if you stay over.
why: The biggest balloon gathering within reach of home, with two Night Glow weekends in a row.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed nine-day format running from the Friday before the first September weekend to the following Saturday (29 Aug-6 Sep 2025, 30 Aug-7 Sep 2024); the official site still shows the 2025 edition and the fetched pages gave no 2026/2027 dates. Verify before planning.

ticketNote: Registration online from early May 2027; fee not yet published
name: 80th Airborne Wandeltocht Oosterbeek
highlights: The world's largest one-day commemorative walk, 35,000 walkers over 10, 15, 25 or 40 km through the Battle of Arnhem landscape, with military bands and detachments in uniform.
tip: Register in May for the 10 or 15 km family route and stay for the bands at the finish.
why: The 80th edition of the Airborne March, walked by military units from across NATO.

train: Lille-Flandres and Lille-Europe stations are in the braderie zone
ticketNote: Free
name: Braderie de Lille
highlights: Europe's largest flea market takes over the whole city for a weekend, with more than 2.5 million visitors in 2026, piles of mussel shells outside every brasserie and a half-marathon on Saturday morning.
tip: Come by train (Lille-Flandres is in the middle of it) and arrive early Saturday; the city centre is closed to cars and parking is impossible.
why: A whole city turned into one giant market and moules-frites party, the biggest street event in France outside Paris.

ticketNote: Museum admission applies
name: Eyewitness Event (living history) Overloon 2027
highlights: Living-history weekend on the museum grounds with re-enactor camps, vehicles and battle demonstrations around the Battle of Overloon anniversary.
tip: Combine with the museum's tank hall; arrive at opening for the demonstrations.
why: A living-history weekend at the country's biggest war museum, an easy day trip.

ticketNote: Free to watch; tank rides paid
dateNote: Annual, the weekend nearest the 2 September liberation anniversary; the organiser's site shows a 2026 edition but no 2027 dates yet.
name: Tanks in Town Mons 2027
highlights: Dozens of running WWII Sherman tanks and other armour gather at Mons for the anniversary of its liberation by the US 3rd Armored Division, with a convoy through the villages on Saturday and the tanks parading onto the Grand-Place on Sunday.
tip: Stand on the Grand-Place for the Sunday afternoon arrival of the Shermans; book a tank ride on the organiser's site.
why: The largest gathering of running Sherman tanks in Europe rolling through a city centre.

name: Corso Zundert 2027
times: Parade on Sunday afternoon; floats parade again on Monday afternoon
ticketNote: Ticketed access to the route; Sunday tickets usually sell out, Monday has more room
highlights: The largest dahlia flower parade in the world: twenty hamlets build 20-metre floats covered in millions of dahlias, pushed by hand through the village with theatre and music on Sunday and again on Monday.
tip: Buy route tickets as soon as they go on sale (Sunday sells out first) and arrive early; the Kindercorso follows two weeks later on the third Sunday of September.
why: The world's biggest flower parade is one of the few Dutch events that genuinely counts as world-renowned, 90 minutes from home.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed pattern (first Sunday of September plus Monday; 2026 edition 6-7 September); official site had not yet listed 2027 at research time.

times: Evening shows 20:00; weekend matinees 14:00 (2026 pattern)
ticketNote: 2026 prices: EUR 42 side stand, EUR 52 main stand
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the 2026 edition (10-13 Sept at the Brabanthallen); the Taptoe moved from Rotterdam Ahoy to 's-Hertogenbosch.
name: Nationale Taptoe 2027
highlights: The Dutch armed forces' military tattoo: massed bands of the army, navy, air force and marechaussee, international guest bands, drill displays, pipes and drums and a grand finale with all performers.
tip: Book the Saturday evening show as soon as sales open; the main stand faces the entrance march.
why: The national military tattoo is a full evening of bands and drill that the whole family enjoys.

dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed pattern (opens on the Friday before the second Sunday of September, two long weekends: 2024 ran 6-10 and 13-16 Sept, 2025 12-16 and 19-22 Sept, 2026 11-15 and 18-21 Sept). Official site was unreachable at research time; confirm on duerkheimer-wurstmarkt.de.
ticketNote: Free entry
name: Dürkheimer Wurstmarkt
highlights: The world's largest wine festival: wine stands and huge wine halls on the Brühlwiesen next to the giant Dürkheimer Fass, a full fairground and fireworks.
tip: Stay overnight or appoint a driver; book accommodation months ahead and come on the second weekend for the closing fireworks.
why: Two weekends of wine, rides and fireworks at the largest wine festival on earth, under three hours away in the Pfalz.
driveNote: Tier 1 radius exception: just over three hours

name: Pützchens Markt Bonn 2027
times: Fri from 12:00, Sat to Tue from 10:00
ticketNote: Free entry, pay per ride
highlights: Bonn's biggest annual event: a five-day fair with some 500 showmen and around 900,000 visitors on the second weekend of September, with the newest travelling rides and a fireworks finale.
tip: Take the tram or S-Bahn from Bonn Hbf, as parking around Pützchen is scarce, and go on the Saturday for the full programme.
why: A large traditional fair 90 minutes away that fits a September day trip with the Rhine.

dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the pattern (second weekend of September; the 2026 edition was 12-13 September at BMCC).
ticketNote: Tasting package bought at the door or online; price not yet published
name: Brugs Bierfestival
highlights: Dozens of Belgian breweries pour hundreds of beers inside the Bruges convention centre, two minutes from the Markt.
tip: Saturday opens at 14:00 and runs late; Sunday 12:00-20:00 is calmer and easier to combine with a walk through the old town.
why: A Belgian beer festival inside one of the most beautiful cities in Europe, close enough for a day trip.

dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed pattern (second weekend of September; 2026 was 12-13 September). Theme not yet announced.
ticketNote: Free
name: Open Monumentendag
highlights: Thousands of monuments across the Netherlands open their doors free of charge for one weekend, including private houses, churches and industrial heritage normally closed to the public.
tip: Check the Maastricht and Heerlen programmes the week before and pick the monuments that are only open this weekend.
why: A free weekend to walk into buildings that are closed the rest of the year.

name: Rhein in Flammen Oberwesel 2027
times: Wine festival during the day, ship convoy and fireworks after dark
venue: Rhine at Oberwesel, Schönburg castle and the town walls
ticketNote: Free from the riverbanks; ship places sold separately
highlights: The Night of a Thousand Fires: Oberwesel's medieval towers and the Schönburg are lit in Bengal fire as the illuminated ship convoy passes and fireworks are fired from the town walls.
tip: Stand on the Kaub side or on the Rhine promenade in Oberwesel, and combine with the town's wine festival that weekend.
why: The most atmospheric Rhein in Flammen, with a whole medieval town lit in red fire.
dateNote: The 2026 Oberwesel edition was cancelled because of low water; 2027 date listed on the official site.

name: International Sanicole Airshow 2027
times: Sat Sunset Airshow 17:00-20:45; Sun main airshow 10:00-17:30
ticketNote: 2027 prices and on-sale date not yet published; the free Sanicole Insider mailing list promises the lowest ticket prices and early access.
highlights: Belgium's biggest civil airshow: a Saturday evening Sunset Airshow with pyrotechnic aerobatics as the sun goes down, then a full Sunday of military jets, display teams and warbirds. Past editions drew the Patrouille de France, Frecce Tricolori, F-16 and F-35 demos and the Red Devils.
tip: Sign up as a Sanicole Insider now for the cheapest tickets, buy the Sunset show separately, and arrive well before 15:00 on Saturday because access roads around the airfield clog up.
parking: Event parking around the airfield; follow signage from the N73 (details published closer to the date).
why: The best airshow within an hour of home, with a sunset pyro show on Saturday and a full military flying display on Sunday.
dateNote: Dates stated on sanicole.com: 11 and 12 September 2027. Note the Sunset Airshow is on the Saturday, not the Friday. A spotters day at the neighbouring Kleine-Brogel air base usually falls on the Friday before (10 Sep 2027) but is only announced by Belgian Defence shortly beforehand.

ticketNote: Free
name: Tag des offenen Denkmals
highlights: Germany's open monument day on Sunday 12 September 2027: thousands of historic sites open free, with Aachen's cathedral precinct and Cologne's Roman and Romanesque heritage within an hour.
tip: Combine it with the Dutch Open Monumentendag weekend and pick Aachen for a short trip across the border.
why: The German counterpart of Open Monumentendag falls on the same weekend, with Aachen half an hour away.

times: Sunday memorial service 11:00 at Arnhem Oosterbeek War Cemetery; Driel Polish commemoration Saturday 15:00; Arnhem Airborne Monument Friday 19:15
venue: Airborne War Cemetery Oosterbeek, Airborneplein Arnhem, Polenplein Driel
ticketNote: Free
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the fixed pattern (weekend around 17 September; 2026 was 17-20 Sept). Programme published in summer 2027.
name: Airborne Commemorations Arnhem-Oosterbeek-Driel 2027 (83rd Battle of Arnhem)
highlights: The commemorative weekend of the Battle of Arnhem: the Sunday memorial service with flower-laying by schoolchildren at the Oosterbeek war cemetery, the Polish commemoration in Driel, pipes and drums on the John Frost Bridge, the Race to the Bridge convoy of WWII vehicles and the White Ribbon Mile silent march.
tip: Base yourself in Oosterbeek, do the Ginkel Heath drop on Saturday and the cemetery service on Sunday morning.
why: A whole weekend of Market Garden ceremonies, convoys and bands around Arnhem, where Nick's profession meets history.

venue: Rijnkade at the John Frost Bridge
ticketNote: Free
dateNote: The organiser counts down to the 2027 edition without a date; projected for the Friday of the Airborne weekend (2026: Friday 18 Sept).
name: Bridge to Liberation Experience 2027
highlights: An open-air commemorative show on a floating stage on the Rhine beneath the John Frost Bridge, telling Battle of Arnhem stories through live music, dance by Introdans and film, broadcast live on NPO.
tip: Be on the Rijnkade by 19:30 for a spot by the water; the pipes and drums march across the bridge just before.
why: A big free spectacle of music, dance and film at the bridge too far, with the city's commemoration weekend around it.

name: Fêtes de Wallonie Namur 2027
times: Concerts and folklore all weekend; Joute de l'Échasse d'Or on Sunday afternoon
venue: Place d'Armes, Place Saint-Aubain and the old town
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Namur's biggest party: free concerts on the squares, folklore groups, the Walloniades, and the UNESCO-listed stilt jousting of the Échasseurs for the Golden Stilt on Sunday.
tip: Go on Sunday for the stilt joust on Place Saint-Aubain and arrive early; the centre is pedestrianised and packed.
train: Namur station, 10 minutes walk
why: Stilt jousting and a whole city partying for free, 90 minutes from home.
dateNote: Official site states the festival falls on the third weekend of September each year (2026 edition ran up to 21 September); 2027 projected as 17-19 September.

name: Musica Sacra Maastricht 2027
venue: Theater aan het Vrijthof, Basilica of Our Lady and churches
ticketNote: General sale usually opens in July (2026: 11 July); per-concert tickets
highlights: A themed weekend of sacred and spiritual music, theatre, film and art in Maastricht's churches and theatre, the 45th edition in 2027.
tip: Concerts in the Basilica of Our Lady are the atmospheric pick; buy early as the churches are small.
why: An intimate festival of sacred music in Maastricht's historic churches, 20 minutes from home.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the third-weekend-of-September pattern (18 to 20 Sep 2026); official site has not announced 2027.

times: Grounds roughly 09:00-16:00; main commemoration late morning (2026: 11:30-12:30)
ticketNote: Free
name: Airborne Luchtlandingen en Herdenking Ginkelse Heide 2027
highlights: Mass parachute drops by hundreds of paratroopers from the Netherlands, UK, US, Poland and other allies from Hercules and other transport aircraft over the original 1944 drop zone, with a commemoration, veterans, flypasts and a ground programme by 11 Air Mobile Brigade.
tip: Arrive before 09:00, use the signed parking and shuttles, bring binoculars and a picnic as the drops run in waves through the day.
why: Hundreds of allied paratroopers jumping over the heath is the most spectacular Market Garden commemoration there is.

name: Lichtjesroute Eindhoven 2027
venue: Signposted driving and cycling route through Eindhoven (about 22 km)
ticketNote: Free
highlights: Since 1945 Eindhoven marks its liberation on 18 September with a 22 km route of illuminated light frames and figures, driven or cycled after dark for three weeks.
tip: Cycle it on a dry weekday evening with the route map from the website, or drive it slowly with the kids in the back.
why: An easy free evening out an hour away that combines lights with the liberation story.
dateNote: Eindhoven tourism page lists the 2027 edition as 18 September to 10 October 2027; the route always opens on 18 September.

name: Rhein in Flammen St. Goar/St. Goarshausen 2027
times: Festival during the day, ship convoy and fireworks after dark
venue: Rhine between St. Goar and St. Goarshausen below the Loreley
ticketNote: Free from the riverbanks; ship places sold separately
highlights: The last Rhein in Flammen of the year: fireworks from Burg Rheinfels, Burg Katz and the Loreley rock over an illuminated ship convoy on the narrowest stretch of the Rhine.
tip: The St. Goarshausen bank gives the view of Rheinfels castle; arrive early as the valley roads jam after the show.
why: Fireworks at the Loreley with two castles in flames, the closing night of the Rhine fireworks season.

ticketNote: 2026 price: EUR 12.50 adults, EUR 7.50 children
dateNote: Projected for the Sunday of the Market Garden weekend (2026: Sunday 20 Sept).
name: Freedom Festival, Freedom Museum Groesbeek 2027
highlights: Family day at the museum on the Market Garden drop zones with WWII jeep and Dodge battlefield tours, veterans' family talks, a children's flea market, the Euregio Freedom Walk and live music.
tip: Book the Grateful Generation jeep tour in advance; combine with the Canadian war cemetery next door.
why: A gentle family way into the Market Garden weekend with jeep rides on the real battlefield.

times: Daytime ceremony at the Waalcrossing monument; Sunset March at sunset on De Oversteek bridge
venue: Waalcrossing monument and De Oversteek bridge
ticketNote: Free
dateNote: Held on the anniversary date 20 September each year; 2027 programme not yet published.
name: Waalcrossing Commemoration and Sunset March Nijmegen 2027
highlights: Wreath-laying with US Army soldiers of the 82nd Airborne and the Dutch and US delegations for the 48 Americans who died crossing the Waal in canvas boats in 1944, followed by the veteran-led Sunset March as the 48 bridge lights come on one by one.
tip: Join the Sunset March at the west end of De Oversteek a few minutes before sunset.
why: A small but powerful American ceremony where Nick's own army is always represented.

times: Royal procession around 13:00, balcony scene around 14:00
dateNote: Prinsjesdag is always the third Tuesday of September per the Royal House; that is 21 September 2027. The 2027 edition is not yet listed on the official page.
ticketNote: Free along the route; grandstand seats are sold separately
name: Prinsjesdag
highlights: The King and Queen ride in the Glass Coach from Noordeinde Palace to the Ridderzaal escorted by mounted guards and military bands, ending with the balcony appearance and a flypast.
tip: Take a spot on the Lange Voorhout or Korte Vijverberg by 11:30 and bring something to stand on; the city centre is closed to cars.
why: A full royal and military procession with cavalry, bands and a flypast, on a weekday you can plan around.

name: Spa Six Hours 2027
ticketNote: Day and weekend passes with paddock access; prices for 2027 not yet published.
highlights: The biggest historic racing weekend on the continent: pre-1966 GT40s, E-Types and Cobras in a six-hour race into the dusk, plus a dozen support grids of historic F1, touring cars and sports cars.
tip: Stay for the Saturday evening finish of the six-hour race when the headlights come on at La Source; the paddock is open all weekend.
why: Hundreds of priceless 1960s racing cars driven flat out on Spa, with an open paddock.

name: Nederlandse Dansdagen 2027
venue: Theater aan het Vrijthof and locations in Maastricht
ticketNote: Per-performance tickets via Ticketmatic; programme in late summer
highlights: A week of Dutch dance premieres, awards and free outdoor dance on the Vrijthof, the national dance showcase held in Maastricht every October.
tip: The free outdoor programme on the Vrijthof is the family part; book the gala night early.
why: The country's main dance festival takes place 20 minutes away with free open-air performances.
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the first-week-of-October pattern (2 to 8 Oct 2026, 3 to 9 Oct 2025); official site has not published 2027 dates.

name: ASML Marathon Eindhoven 2027
venue: City centre, finish near the Stadhuisplein
ticketNote: Free to watch; running entries via the organiser.
highlights: A full weekend of running in Eindhoven: kids runs and the 10 km on Saturday, the half and full marathon on Sunday through the city centre.
tip: Stand near the finish on the Stadhuisplein for the atmosphere, or let the kids run the Saturday mini marathon.
why: The closest big-city marathon, an hour away, with runs the kids can join.

name: Monster Energy FIM Motocross of Nations 2027 Assen
times: Qualifying races Saturday 9 Oct, three finals Sunday 10 Oct
venue: TT Circuit Assen (sand track on the circuit infield)
ticketNote: Weekend tickets on sale via Weezevent; prices not listed on the organiser page.
highlights: The 80th edition of the Olympics of motocross: 40 national teams, the world's best riders in one place, and the Dutch team on home sand in front of 60,000 fans.
tip: Bring ear protection and boots, stand on the tribunes at the start straight for the gate drop, and arrive early on Sunday because the three finals run from midday.
why: The once-in-a-decade chance to see motocross's World Cup on Dutch soil.
driveNote: Tier 1 radius exception: just over three hours

name: TCS Amsterdam Marathon 2027
times: Start 09:00 at the Olympic Stadium
venue: Olympic Stadium start and finish, Amstel river loop
ticketNote: Free to watch; running entries sell out months ahead.
highlights: A world-class fast marathon that starts and finishes on the track of the 1928 Olympic Stadium and loops along the Amstel, with 45,000 runners across the distances.
tip: Sit in the Olympic Stadium stands for the finish; the stadium is free to enter on race day.
lez: Amsterdam has a low-emission zone for older diesels; check your plate online.
why: A marathon finish inside an Olympic stadium, free to watch.
dateNote: 2027 date projected from the fixed third-Sunday-of-October pattern (18 October 2026); the organiser site did not respond from this session.

name: Amsterdam Dance Event 2027
ticketNote: Pre-register for pre-sale access; individual club events ticketed separately, most 18+
highlights: The world's largest electronic music conference and festival with 1,000 events in 200 venues over five days and nights.
tip: Pick two or three big-room shows (Ziggo Dome, Gashouder) and book them the day they go on sale; stay in the city.
why: A city-wide dance music takeover for a weekend in Amsterdam, the global reference event in its genre.

name: Atelier Fernand Léger (Kunstsammlung NRW)
times: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00, closed Monday
ticketNote: K20 collection and exhibition €17, under 18 free (current price)
highlights: Autumn 2027 exhibition on Fernand Léger's studio and the machine-age modernism of his tubular figures, listed in the NRW tourism board's exhibition preview.
tip: Not yet on the museum site; check kunstsammlung.de in summer 2027 for the venue (K20 or K21) and time-slot booking.
train: Düsseldorf Hbf then U-Bahn to Heinrich-Heine-Allee
dateNote: Dates from the official NRW tourism board listing; the museum has not yet published the exhibition page.
why: The big autumn 2027 modern art show in NRW, for the end of the planning horizon.

train: Eindhoven Centraal, then shuttle buses
ticketNote: Day and multi-day passes online; 2027 prices not yet published
name: Dutch Design Week
highlights: Nine days of exhibitions by thousands of designers across the city, from Strijp-S warehouses to the Design Academy graduation show, with light installations and open studios.
tip: Buy a day pass, start at Strijp-S in the morning and use the free shuttle buses between the clusters; weekdays are far quieter.
why: Northern Europe's biggest design event, seventy minutes away and genuinely interesting for a teenager.

dateNote: 2027 fall dates projected from the pattern (last weekend of October / first of November; the 2026 edition was 31 October-1 November at Flanders Expo). A spring edition usually also runs in April.
name: FACTS Convention Gent (fall edition)
highlights: Belgium's biggest pop-culture convention: film and series actors, cosplay, comics, gaming, K-pop and anime halls at Flanders Expo.
tip: Buy day tickets online in advance and arrive at opening; Saturday is the big cosplay day.
why: The largest comic con in Belgium is a natural fan-event weekend for Alma.

dateNote: 2027 date projected from the fixed pattern (first Saturday of November; 2026 was 7 November).
ticketNote: Single ticket for all museums; sells out almost every year
name: Museumnacht Amsterdam
highlights: Dozens of Amsterdam museums open until 2:00 with DJs, performances and workshops on one ticket.
tip: Buy tickets the day they go on sale in early autumn and plan a route of four or five museums close together.
why: A night of museums turned into clubs is the kind of teen-friendly spectacle Alma would enjoy.

venue: Bastogne War Museum and town centre
ticketNote: Free (museum activities free except the immersive experiences)
dateNote: 2027 dates projected from the pattern (2025: 12-14 Dec, 2026: 11-13 Dec, second weekend of December); not yet announced.
name: Nuts Weekend Bastogne 2027 (Battle of the Bulge commemoration)
highlights: Annual December commemoration of the Siege of Bastogne with military vehicle convoys, living-history camps, battlefield walks and the nut-throwing town parade.
tip: Check bastognewarmuseum.be from November for the programme; the Saturday parade is the highlight.
why: Bastogne's Battle of the Bulge weekend is the Ardennes' biggest WWII commemoration and only 90 minutes from home.
